name: QT-Opt
summary: QT-Opt is a scalable distributed Q-learning method using the cross-entropy method for continuous action selection, trained on 580k real grasp attempts collected over months by seven robots. It reached 96% success on unseen objects and, more interestingly, produced emergent behaviors nobody scripted: singulating cluttered objects, repositioning for a better grip, and retrying after failure.
innovation: Distributed off-policy Q-learning at a data scale nobody had attempted on real hardware.
Showed closed-loop RL grasping beats open-loop predict-then-execute pipelines.
matters: The proof that real-robot RL scales with data, and the ancestor of Google's whole robot-learning program.
limits: Enormous data cost for one task family; the robot farm was not reproducible outside Google.
lineage: Large-scale value-based RL, later fused with transformers in Q-Transformer.
